_note: Advanced V2 concept questions for heaps.

questions.title: Heap root
questions.prompt: A max-heap stores priorities 7, 5, 3, and 2. Which value must be at the root?
questions.explanation: In a max-heap, the root is the largest priority because every parent is at least as large as its children.

questions.title: Insert bubble-up
questions.code:
Before insert: [7, 5, 3]
Append 9 as newest leaf:
[7, 5, 3, 9]

parent of 9 = 5
questions.prompt: After inserting priority 9 into a max-heap whose root is 7, what has to happen?
choices: 9 compares with parents and can move upward
9 stays at the newest leaf forever
Every value must be sorted left to right
questions.explanation: Insertion starts at a leaf, then swaps upward until the parent rule is true again.

questions.title: Remove priority
questions.prompt: Why does removing from a heap usually move the last item to the root first?
choices: It fills the empty root before bubbling down
It sorts the whole array immediately
It deletes every child of the root
questions.explanation: The last array slot is cheap to remove. Moving it to the root restores the shape, then bubbling down restores priority order.

questions.title: Complete shape
questions.prompt: Which heap property keeps the array representation simple?
choices: The tree is filled level by level
Every node has exactly two children
questions.explanation: A heap is a complete tree, so parent and child indexes can be calculated without node pointers.

questions.title: Min-heap choice
questions.prompt: A scheduler needs the smallest wait time first. Which heap direction fits best?
questions.explanation: A min-heap keeps the smallest priority at the root, so the next shortest wait is quick to remove.

questions.title: Parent check
questions.prompt: Parent priority is 4 and a new child priority is 8 in a max-heap. What should the insert step do?
choices: Convert the heap to a queue
questions.explanation: For a max-heap, a child with priority 8 breaks the parent rule under 4, so it must move upward.

questions.title: When heaps fit
questions.prompt: Which problem is a natural heap problem?
choices: Check whether a word is a palindrome
Count characters in a short string
questions.explanation: Heaps are strongest when the next highest or lowest priority must be retrieved many times.

questions.title: Heap mistake
questions.prompt: What is a common mistake when reading a heap stored in an array?
choices: Assuming siblings are sorted with each other
Comparing a child with its parent
questions.explanation: A heap orders parents against children, but siblings do not have to be sorted left to right.
